subject: Remove repeated source compilation and lowering from hosted database qualification
claim: Five ordinary hosted construction functions now share one uncached source-build, lowering, and object-admission routine per host. The Windows HostStorage and dependent HostRootWriter behaviors passed. HostStorage changed from 132970 ms to 129620 ms; this small single-observation difference under different concurrent load does not establish a reliable speedup. Linking and packaging remain the next cost to isolate. No complete database or cross-host qualification is claimed.

limitations: Windows behavior and static routing/syntax checks passed. The record remains incomplete because the Debian runtime attempt exceeded its bound and supplies no passing Linux execution evidence.

The before/after observations used retained qualified tool artifacts and freshly constructed test products. These are not clean-machine measurements. The revised Windows run overlapped routing verification and a Debian attempt; do not treat its small timing difference as a performance improvement.

Complete database qualification, the remaining hosted behavior cases, complete dual-host qualification, and broad compiler/lowerer suites were not run because they exceed the remaining ten-minute local development budget and are unnecessary for the narrow extraction evidence.

Compiler and lowerer reproducibility are delegated to the existing focused qualification owners and the retained paired database StorageLowering case. Per-project hosted A/B comparisons are deliberately removed; no claim is made that each database product was independently reconstructed twice.
Both target packages and common-host assembly reproducibility remain constructed as before. Duplicate host packaging and repeated cross-case products remain optimization work.
Peak child-process working-set memory was not measured. The routing-verifier process reported a 222486528-byte peak working set. No stable timing or memory regression threshold is established.
